standard.title: Fundamental Movement Skills
standard.description: practise fundamental movement skills in minor game and play situations
standard.prior_knowledge: No prior HPE curriculum. Students bring informal movement experience from play and daily life — walking, running, throwing, catching — but without structured FMS practice.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students practise locomotor, object-manipulation and balance skills in minor game and play situations, combining them with increasing control and purpose.

nodes.label: Locomotor skills in play
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply different locomotor skills (walking, running, jumping, hopping, skipping) to move purposefully from one point to another in a play context.
nodes.minimum_width: Move between two points using at least two different locomotor skills in a simple game or activity.
nodes.typical_width: Apply a range of locomotor skills (at least four) in minor games and imaginative play; demonstrate basic control of starting, stopping and changing direction.
wider: Apply locomotor skills in natural and outdoor environments, adapting movement to uneven terrain or open space
Combine locomotor sequences (e.g. run–jump–hop) in response to game signals or teacher cues
Explore locomotor skills used in First Nations Australian games such as running-based chasing games
nodes.hinge_reason: Locomotor control underpins safe participation in all subsequent FMS combinations. Students who cannot move purposefully between points struggle with every minor game context in this standard and in the Y1-2 band.

response_modes.reason: Foundation students need repeated practice across varied play contexts before locomotor patterns become reliable. Precision of starting, stopping and direction changes should be emphasised before combining with object manipulation.
Vary the play contexts (chasing games, imaginative play, natural environments) to build transferable locomotor control across settings.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Locomotor skills in varied settings — outdoor, culturally situated, rhythmically organised — offer rich physical literacy opportunities beyond mere skill consolidation.
success_criteria: Applies at least two different locomotor skills during a game or play activity
Moves with basic control, including stopping and changing direction when needed

nodes.label: Object manipulation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can send, control and receive objects (rolling, throwing, catching, kicking) in different ways and at different levels.
nodes.minimum_width: Practise at least one sending skill (throw or kick) and one receiving skill (catch or stop) using a ball or similar object.
nodes.typical_width: Practise a range of object manipulation skills — throwing, catching, rolling, kicking — in minor games; send and receive objects at different heights and distances.
wider: Explore sending and receiving objects using non-standard equipment (scarves, beanbags, balloons) to isolate tracking and timing
Practise water confidence skills such as floating with a buoyancy aid and receiving objects in/near water
Combine object manipulation with locomotion in simple game structures (e.g. carry-and-pass relay)
nodes.hinge_reason: Object manipulation skill is a prerequisite for most minor game and sports contexts in Y1-2. Students with very limited manipulation experience cannot access game structures that form the basis of later FMS progression.

response_modes.reason: Fine and gross motor patterns for throwing and catching require repeated, low-pressure practice. Use varied equipment sizes and distances to build consistency before applying in game contexts.
Different equipment types (balloon, beanbag, ball) and environments (pool, outdoor) broaden manipulation experience and reveal transfer gaps.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Non-standard equipment and aquatic contexts expose students to tracking, timing and body orientation challenges absent from standard ball-game practice.
success_criteria: Demonstrates at least one sending skill and one receiving skill with a manipulable object
Attempts to adjust body position to send or receive the object at different heights or distances

nodes.label: Weight transfer and balance
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can transfer weight from one body part to another with control, and demonstrate basic balance in still and moving positions.
nodes.minimum_width: Demonstrate one weight-transfer sequence (e.g. roll, cartwheel attempt, or step-and-balance) with basic control.
nodes.typical_width: Practise a range of weight-transfer movements — rolling, rocking, stepping patterns, simple gymnastic sequences; hold balance positions on different body bases.
wider: Explore weight transfer and balance on natural surfaces and equipment (logs, slopes, uneven ground)
Combine balance sequences with locomotion in movement stories or creative play contexts
Explore fine motor combining tasks: threading, stacking or building activities that develop hand-coordination alongside gross motor balance

response_modes.reason: Weight transfer and balance require body awareness that develops through repeated exploratory practice — not from a single lesson. Low-stakes, playful contexts are most effective at Foundation.

success_criteria: Transfers weight from one body part to another in a practised sequence
Holds a balance position on at least one body base with brief stillness

nodes.label: FMS in minor games
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can combine locomotor, manipulation and balance skills in minor game and play situations with purpose and enjoyment.
nodes.minimum_width: Participate in at least one minor game that requires combining two or more FMS (e.g. running and catching, or skipping and kicking).
nodes.typical_width: Participate in a range of minor games that combine locomotor, object-manipulation and balance skills; apply skills with increasing control and adapt to game demands.
wider: Apply FMS in First Nations Australian game contexts, comparing game structures with other minor games experienced
Apply FMS skills in natural and outdoor environments with varying terrain and conditions
Participate in games combining multiple skill types simultaneously (e.g. run, dodge, send) in progressively more complex play structures

response_modes.reason: This node is the integration point — locomotor, manipulation and balance skills are combined in game contexts. Teacher investment here is in facilitating game structures that demand skill combination, not isolated skill repetition.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: First Nations game contexts and varied outdoor environments are pedagogically rich — they situate FMS in culturally and environmentally meaningful contexts beyond the gymnasium or court.
success_criteria: Participates in a minor game that requires combining two or more movement skills
Applies fundamental movement skills with intent — moves in response to game demands, not randomly
